stages.title: LANDLOCKED PENALTY AND ROUTE POSITION

HIGHER FREIGHT COST, LONGER TRANSIT, NO INDEPENDENT TRADE GUARANTEE
TRANSIT AGREEMENTS AND CORRIDOR PROJECTS GAIN DISPROPORTIONATE WEIGHT
ROUTE POSITION ON A LANE OR LAND BRIDGE OFTEN
SITUATION IS RELATIVE; A NEW CANAL, CORRIDOR OR CLOSURE

CONSEQUENCE → higher freight cost, longer transit, no independent trade guarantee
RESPONSE → transit agreements and corridor projects gain disproportionate weight
CONTRAST → route position on a lane or land bridge often outweighs endowment
CAUTION → situation is relative; a new canal, corridor or closure rewrites it

NOT: Country-capital questions are enough - UPSC increasingly combines country with strait, sea, river, plateau, delta or island chain .
